boilerplate.section_intro: This section consists of questions and problems involving quantitative reasoning.  Each question is followed by four possible responses.  Choose the correct answer and mark its number in the appropriate place on the answer sheet.
boilerplate.section_meta:
This section contains 20 questions.
The time allotted is 20 minutes.
boilerplate.gray_note: Note:  The words appearing against a gray background are translated into several languages at the bottom of each page.
boilerplate.general_comments_title: General Comments about the Quantitative Reasoning Section
general_comments: The figures accompanying some of the problems are provided to help solve the problems, but are not necessarily drawn to scale.  Therefore, do not rely on the figures alone to deduce line length, angle size, and so forth.
If a line in a figure appears to be straight, you may assume that it is in fact a straight line.
When a geometric term (side, radius, area, volume, etc.) appears in a problem, it refers to a term whose value is greater than 0, unless stated otherwise.
When \(\sqrt{a}\) (a > 0) appears in a problem, it refers to the positive root of a.
"0" is neither a positive nor a negative number.

clusters.intro:
Study the graph below, then answer the five questions that follow.

13 runners participated in a running competition on a course whose length was 3,000 meters.
The graphs detail the running data of two of the runners: Amnon and Boaz.
On the horizontal axes nine time periods are marked: the first eight are time periods of one minute each, and the ninth time period is the last seconds of the run.  For each time period, on the lower horizontal axis is given the distance that the runner passed from the beginning of the course until the end of the time period.
For each time period a rectangle corresponds: the ends of the rectangle indicate the runner's relative position among all the runners at the beginning of the time period and at its end (see key).  A light rectangle indicates that the runner improved his position and a dark rectangle indicates that the runner worsened his position.
Note: The relative position of a runner during some time period is any position between his position at the beginning of the time period and his position at the end of the time period, and he does not deviate from these positions.

For example: The sixth time period began 5 minutes after the beginning of the run.  At the beginning of this time period Boaz's relative position was 7, and at its end his relative position was 6.  In total Boaz passed 370 meters in this minute (370 = 1,710 – 2,080).

Study the graph below, then answer the four questions that follow.

The graph relates to the forces of the American army that arrived in France in the First World War from June 1917 until October 1918.
The forces are composed of divisions, and each division has a different identifying number.  The graph indicates the identifying numbers of all the divisions that were in France in each month.  Each row in the graph presents a different division.

Note: In the entire period described in the graph no division left France.

For example, in the month of September 1917 there were three American divisions in France: division 1, division 2 and division 26.  This was the first month in which division 26 was in France.

The sum of three consecutive numbers is 33.

The product of the two greatest numbers among them is:

methods.text: Three consecutive numbers are symmetric about the middle one, so their sum is three times the middle: the middle is 11, and the numbers are 10, 11, 12.
The two greatest are 11 and 12, whose product is 132. The trap is multiplying 10 and 11 instead, which gives 110 — also on the option list.

questions.stem:
In a certain kibbutz there are 9 volunteers who work in agriculture:

- 5 volunteers who work in collecting eggs and in vegetable picking only
- 3 volunteers who work in milking and in vegetable picking only
- 1 volunteer who works in collecting eggs and in milking only

What is the ratio between the number of volunteers who work in milking and the number of volunteers who work in vegetable picking?

methods.text: Count each task: milking has \(3+1 = 4\) volunteers, vegetable picking has \(5+3 = 8\). The ratio is \(1:2\).
Each volunteer is counted in two tasks, so the task totals exceed 9. That is expected, not an error.

questions.stem: The total number of letters that a mailman distributed is equal to the number of letters that he distributed on average to each house  ______  the number of houses in which he distributed letters.

From 9 overlapping parallelograms a large parallelogram was formed, as described in the figure.
The perimeter of each one of the small parallelograms is a cm.

What is the perimeter of the large parallelogram (in cm)?

Given: x + y = 3
     y ≤ -2

What is the exact range of x ?

methods.text: Substitute \(x=3-y\). Since \(y\le-2\), \(-y\ge2\), so \(x=3+(-y)\ge5\).
\(x\) is 3 minus \(y\), so \(x\) is smallest when \(y\) is largest. The largest \(y\) is allowed to be is \(-2\), which puts \(x\) at 5 — and \(y\) has no lower bound, so \(x\) has no upper one.

questions.stem: A square whose side length is 2 meters is drawn on a playground. Anat is standing on one of the corners of the square and begins to walk along its perimeter. At each step she can continue in the same direction or go back. The length of each step of Anat is one meter. Which of the following distances cannot be the distance of Anat (in a straight line) from her starting point after 4 steps?

Two workers work in fields, each one at his own constant rate: Worker A plows a field whose area is 1 dunam in 15 hours. Worker B plows a field whose area is 1 dunam in 10 hours. The two workers required 30 hours in order to plow a certain field together. What is the area of this field (in dunams)?

methods.text: Combined rate \(\frac1{15} + \frac1{10} = \frac16\) dunam an hour. In 30 hours that is 5 dunams.
Rates in dunams per hour add directly, so no conversion is needed — the two given times share a unit by design.

Given: x , y , z , w > 1

The expression \(\dfrac{\dfrac{x}{y}}{\dfrac{z}{w}}\) is -

methods.text: The expression is \(\dfrac{x/y}{z/w} = \dfrac{xw}{yz}\). \(x\) and \(w\) are on top, \(y\) and \(z\) underneath, so increasing \(y\) decreases the value — option (3).
Start from \(x=y=z=w=2\), value 1, and change one letter at a time. Raising \(y\) to 4 halves it; raising \(x\) or lowering \(w\) or \(z\) moves it the other way from what the other options claim.

questions.stem:
Given: a > 1

\(\dfrac{1-a}{1+\sqrt{a}} = ?\)

methods.text: \(1-a\) is a difference of squares in the roots: \(1-a = (1-\sqrt a)(1+\sqrt a)\). The second bracket is the denominator, so it cancels and \(1-\sqrt a\) is left.
\(a=9\): the stem is \(\frac{-8}{4} = -2\), and \(1-\sqrt9 = -2\). The others give \(-12\), 6 and \(-3\).

questions.stem:
a and b are positive integers.
Given: a = 3b

Which of the following numbers can a + b be ?

methods.text: \(a = 3b\), so \(a + b = 4b\) — always a multiple of 4.
Test each option for divisibility by 4 using the last two digits: \(26\), \(62\), \(21\), \(84\). Only \(84\) is divisible by 4, so only 484 qualifies.

\(\dfrac{a^8 \cdot c^3}{a^4 \cdot c^6} = ?\)  ,  (a , c ≠ 0)

methods.text: Subtract exponents base by base: \(a^{8-4} = a^4\) and \(c^{3-6} = c^{-3}\).

questions.stem: In the store "Hamalbish" the price of trousers is 75 shekels and the price of a shirt is 45 shekels. On a certain day the number of shirts that were sold was 3 times as much as the number of trousers that were sold. The total of all the money that was received from selling shirts and trousers on that day was 840 shekels. How many trousers were sold in the store on that day?

An elevator in a certain building goes up at a rate of 5 floors per minute and goes down at a rate of 10 floors per minute.

How much time will be required for the elevator to go up from floor 5 to floor 25, after that to go down to floor 15, and at the end to go up to floor 40 (without stops)?

methods.text: Multi-phase accounting, one leg at a time: 20 floors up at 5 a minute is 4 minutes; 10 down at 10 a minute is 1; then the final leg.
Up and down have different rates, so the legs cannot be combined into a single distance. Counting floors travelled, not floors numbered, is the other half of it.

questions.stem: In the period described in the graph, which of the following divisions was in France the most time?

After the war (from the month of November 1918 onwards) they began to evacuate the American divisions from France at a rate of 3 divisions per month.  The order of the evacuation was determined according to the seniority of the divisions in France: at first the first 3 divisions that arrived in France were evacuated, in the following month the 3 divisions that arrived after them were evacuated, and so on.

After 8 months of evacuation, it is possible that the most veteran division that was on French soil was division -
Which of the following statements is true regarding the months described in the graph?
options: There is a month in which no division arrived in France
There is a month in which more than 10 divisions arrived in France
In every month at least 2 divisions arrived in France
In every month more divisions arrived in France than in the month before it

questions.stem: A history teacher calculated how many divisions on average were added to the forces in France in each month during the period described in the graph (assuming that the first division arrived in June 1917).  The average that the teacher received is a number -

Given: a is equal to 50% of b.
     c is equal to 125% of b.

Therefore, c is equal to  ______  of a.

methods.text: Set \(b = 100\): \(a = 50\) and \(c = 125\). Then \(c\) as a percentage of \(a\) is \(\frac{125}{50} = 250\%\).
Or divide the two multipliers: \(\frac{1.25}{0.5} = 2.5\). Routing both through \(b\) is what makes a direct comparison possible.

questions.stem:
Two fair game dice are tossed.

\(\dfrac{\text{the probability that the sum of the results of the toss will be 12}}{\text{the probability that the sum of the results of the toss will be 11}} = ?\)

a, b and c are three numbers that are different from 0.

Given: | a | + b + | c | = c

Which of the following statements is necessarily true?

methods.text: Rearrange for \(b\): \(b=c-|c|-|a|\). The part \(c-|c|\) is 0 when \(c\) is positive and \(2c\) when negative — never positive. And \(-|a|\) is strictly negative, since \(a\ne0\). So \(b<0\).
\(|c|\) is at least \(c\) and \(|a|\) is strictly above 0, so moving both to the other side can only push \(b\) below zero. Nothing about the individual sign of \(c\) is ever pinned.
\(a=1,\ c=5\) gives \(b=-1\) ✓, and \(a=1,\ c=-5\) gives \(b=-11\) ✓. Since \(c\) works out both positive and negative, options (3) and (4) are both dead.

A, B and C are letters representing digits between 1 and 9.

Given:  35A × 4B = 15CC5

Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
options: A + B is an odd number
A + B is an even number

methods.text: Work on the units digit alone. The product ends in 5, and \(A \times B\) must therefore end in 5 — which needs one of them to be 5 and the other odd.
Test the possibilities against the size of the product: \(355 \times 45 = 15975\) ✓ fits the pattern \(15CC5\) with \(C=9\). So \(A=5,\ B=5\) and \(A+B=10\), which is even.

questions.stem: x, y and z are positive integers. Given: x > y x and y are divisible by z without a remainder. Which of the following statements necessarily holds?

methods.text: \(y\) is a positive multiple of \(z\), so \(y \ge z\). And \(x\) is a multiple of \(z\) strictly greater than \(y\), so it is at least the next multiple up: \(x \ge 2z\).
The others fall to one case each. \(z=3,\ y=3,\ x=9\) has \(z = y\), killing (1), and \(x \ne 2y\), killing (2). And \(z=3,\ y=6,\ x=9\) has \(y > z\), killing (4).
